faqs.question: What is the best email marketing software?
faqs.answer: The best choice depends on list size, sending frequency, automation complexity, integrations, consent requirements and who will maintain the system. Test a representative campaign and automation in each finalist before deciding.

faqs.question: How should I compare email marketing prices?
faqs.answer: Compare the same contact count, monthly send volume, user count, automation requirements, integrations and support level. Include overages and required add-ons, and verify current billing terms with each vendor.

faqs.question: What deliverability checks matter?
faqs.answer: Confirm support for domain authentication such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC, suppression handling, bounce reporting, unsubscribe management and consent records. Deliverability also depends on list quality and sending practices, not only the platform.

body:
Best Email Marketing Software: A Practical Buyer Guide

Email marketing platforms vary in how they manage subscribers, segment audiences, automate journeys, support consent and report campaign results. A useful shortlist starts with your sending workflow and compliance needs, rather than a universal rating. PilotStack has not independently verified current pricing, user ratings or every plan-specific feature in this guide; confirm these details with each vendor before purchase.

Platforms to evaluate

ActiveCampaign: Consider evaluating it when segmentation and automation are important alongside campaign sending. Test the triggers, branching logic, reporting and integrations you need, and confirm which capabilities are included in the quoted plan.

Kit (formerly ConvertKit): Consider it for creator-oriented newsletters and audience workflows. Verify the current product name, subscriber and sending limits, automation options, and the way subscriber data can be exported.

Mailchimp: Evaluate campaign creation, audience management and reporting against your workflow. Pay particular attention to contact-count billing, duplicate or unsubscribed contacts, sending limits and automation availability.

Adobe Marketo Engage: Consider an enterprise evaluation when B2B lead management and complex automation justify a more involved implementation. Ask for a scoped demonstration covering data model, integrations, administration and onboarding effort.

Buyer checklist

  • Campaign editor, reusable templates and approval workflow.
  • Segmentation by consent, engagement, source and customer attributes.
  • Automation triggers, branching, suppression and frequency controls.
  • Domain authentication, bounce handling, unsubscribe and suppression management.
  • Reporting for delivery, clicks, conversions and exports.
  • Integrations with CRM, ecommerce, forms and analytics.
  • Role-based access, data retention and subscriber export.

Test before switching

Use a test audience to build one campaign, one segment and one automation. Check preview and mobile rendering, suppression behavior, unsubscribe processing, reporting latency and how easily data can be exported. Do not send unsolicited campaigns or upload a list unless you have an appropriate legal basis and permission to use it.

Compare total cost

Request pricing for the same contact volume, send volume, number of users, automation needs, integrations and support. Clarify whether unsubscribed contacts count toward billing, what happens when limits are exceeded, and whether onboarding or advanced reporting costs extra. Prices and packaging change, so verify them directly instead of relying on old comparison tables.

Make the decision

Score each finalist against the same must-have requirements. Document gaps and the effort required to maintain the platform. Choose based on list management, automation fit, deliverability controls, reporting and total cost—not an unverified star rating.
